summary:
ASTRA – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System
Team: ASTERIONS

ASTRA is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring platform designed to improve health observation and data accessibility during space missions. It aims to integrate information from multiple sources, including wearable biomedical sensors, external medical instruments and manual inputs.

The proposed system can monitor parameters such as heart rate, SpO₂, ECG, body temperature and physical activity. Modern embedded processors and microcontrollers can collect and process sensor data before presenting it through a unified digital dashboard.

By combining AI-assisted analysis with edge computing, ASTRA aims to make health information easier to understand while supporting faster identification of unusual patterns. Its proposed offline architecture could enable local data processing, storage and basic alerts even without internet connectivity, with synchronisation when communication becomes available.

ASTRA stands out through its multi-input architecture, integrated monitoring approach and potential for hardware expansion. It aims to reduce manual data consolidation, save valuable time and improve access to astronaut health information.

Currently developed as a software prototype, ASTRA has future potential for wearable sensor integration, advanced embedded systems and offline monitoring.

ASTRA – Monitoring Beyond Earth. Protecting Every Mission.
details:
ASTRA is an integrated astronaut health monitoring platform designed to collect and present health-related information through a unified digital interface. It supports multiple input methods, including wearable biomedical sensors, compatible medical instruments and manual entries.

The proposed system focuses on parameters such as heart rate, SpO₂, ECG, body temperature and physical activity. Collected data can be processed and displayed through the ASTRA dashboard, while AI-assisted analysis aims to help identify unusual patterns and provide accessible health insights.

Our current software prototype was developed using Google AI Studio and Gemini, with AI-assisted coding. According to our GitHub repository, the codebase primarily uses TypeScript (97.7%), along with CSS (1.8%) and HTML (0.5%).

ASTRA's future hardware architecture could incorporate ESP32 or STM32 microcontrollers, biomedical sensors and edge computing to enable local processing, offline storage and basic alerts.

Its creativity lies in combining multiple data sources, AI-assisted interpretation and an expandable monitoring architecture. We considered astronaut safety, reliability, time efficiency, accessibility and connectivity limitations during development.

Our intended impact is to reduce manual data consolidation, improve access to health information and support more efficient astronaut health monitoring during space missions.
